The original name of Flagstaff, Arizona is Low's Camp, after Joseph Low, an early settler and guide. The area was later renamed Flagstaff after a large wooden mast (about 20 feet tall) that was planted there and flown with a flag in 1863 (or around that time) to serve as a landmark for emigrants and railroads.    According to historical records from the National Park Service and local histories: The site was first known as "Low's Camp". In 1858, a group of travelers led by Joseph Low established a camp there. Later, in 1863, a flagpole was erected there by emigrants on the Overland Trail. The name "Flagstaff" stuck because of this mast. It was officially incorporated as Flagstaff in 1876.
